eps.d: Ruth, Caralyn and Leigh meet their new neighbour, Charlie, for the first time; but is Ruth as boring as she seems, and just how well does Charlie know her?
Leigh and Caralyn befriend a pair of men who appear slightly oafish, but own a large yacht. Ruth fails to find a man at all, and Charlie is in a relationship he can't get out of!
Charlie is heartbroken when his beloved is taken from him. Meanwhile, Leigh's boyfriend seems to have taken a shine to Ruth, and Caralyn's been spotted out in Hyde Park...
Ruth is particularly unimpressed with the new woman in Charlie's life, whilst Caralyn and Leigh battle a broken toilet.

The boiler at Benito's house explodes, and - much to his regret - Charlie offers to put him up. Over in number 23, Ruth and Leigh aren't getting on too well, and Caralyn is distraught at the news of a relationship that she didn't even know about, is ending.

Caralyn arrives home with a kitten, but his presence causes a little upset between the flatmates. Even more upset, however, is Charlie; his ex-wife has been gloating about her good fortune and wonderful relationship.

Ruth has married and moved out; new flatmate Frankie's aspirations of supermodel status lead her to consider breast reduction surgery. Meanwhile, Nick - whose yacht-invading antics once lead Leigh to a police cell - has turned up again and is after her attention.

Caralyn is distraught to find that she has - literally - killed a man with sex. Charlie's paranoid as the man was only his age, and Frankie's attitude to Leigh and Nick's relationship is less than positive.

An invitation to a school reunion in Worthing leaves Caralyn somewhat nervous of the woman who once stole her boyfriend. Back in London, Charlie is providing Benito some emotional support at an open audition session for Stars In Their Eyes .

Leigh catches Nick in bed with another woman: Frankie and Caralyn decide she needs setting up. Charlie is, as ever, busy trying to impress a woman he spotted in the bar. Unfortunately, she's a fitness fanatic.

Charlie and his ex-wife, Angela, make a brief rekindle of their romance. At the flat the girls discuss who Leigh would most fancy if she were a lesbian, and go on to make a video with Charlie's camera.
The company that owns Bar Coda is sending a rep to assess its profitability and performance. He's known as 'The Executioner', but is he as mean as he sounds, and how might his decision be swayed?
Charlie and the girls return to the flat, only to find the door open and a burglar inside. Performing a citizen's arrest, they sit in wait for the police to arrive.
